title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with a synthetic video of a public figure. The deepfake did not fail on its own terms, it did what it was built to do: present a familiar face on a live call so the person on the other end would accept the identity. The harm came from the surrounding human chain, a supposed manager requesting fees and a supposed CBI officer demanding a fine, not from any defect in the generated video.

The deployment surface was a consumer messaging app, outside any controlled or monitored setting. Nothing in the reporting indicates the platform detected or flagged the call, and no verification step stood between the caller's claim of office and the payments. Catching this would have required either a provenance signal attached to the video that a recipient could check, or a verification channel for claims of government aid that does not run through the same call that makes the claim. Neither is described as present.

The reporting is from a single outlet and describes a police case registered under the Information Technology Act. That a case was registered is not a finding of guilt against any identified person, and the identity and intent of those behind the call are not established.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller, speaking Hindi, offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would handle the transfer. The manager then demanded fees, starting with Rs 5,000, followed by Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN. Another person posing as a CBI officer demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh in total before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Fraudsters sent Giri a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh had been allotted to him and identity proof supposedly belonging to a CBI officer. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims.
